reason: Start with glucose absorption to trace its route toward the liver.
expectation: Glucose will cross the villus lining and enter or approach its blood vessels, though the intermediate steps are unclear.

alternatives.reason: Fat absorption is also a goal, but I would follow the glucose route first.

effect: Glucose has crossed an intestinal cell into a capillary; its onward route to the liver remains to be shown.
reaction: The crossing is clear, though the transport mechanism is not explained.
reason: Follow the other nutrient destined for the liver across the villus.
expectation: Amino acids will cross the intestinal lining and enter villus blood, possibly by a different transport mechanism.

alternatives.reason: Fat absorption is also needed, but I want to finish the blood-bound nutrients first.

effect: Both glucose and amino acids have reached villus blood; their route onward remains to be shown.
reaction: The parallel crossings are clear, but neither transport mechanism is explained.
reason: Combine the two blood-borne nutrients to continue tracing their shared route toward the liver.
expectation: The combined nutrients will travel together in blood, possibly toward the liver.

alternatives.reason: Fat absorption is also needed, but I want to follow the blood route first.

effect: Glucose and amino acids now travel in portal blood toward the liver, completing that goal; fat remains.
reaction: The shared blood route is clear, though combining the nutrients felt like a bookkeeping step.
reason: Begin tracing the fat digestion products across the intestinal villus.
expectation: Fat digestion products will enter intestinal cells, likely before being packaged for lymph transport.

alternatives.reason: Packaging materials will probably be needed, but I want to follow the fat into the villus first.

effect: Fatty acids and monoglycerides are inside the intestinal cells; packaging is the next apparent step toward lymph.
reaction: The route is clear so far, though the crossing mechanism remains unexplained.
reason: Package the absorbed fat for its onward route into lymph.
expectation: The intestinal cells will use the materials to package fat into lipoprotein particles; the details are uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The lacteal entrance will likely be needed, but packaging seems to come first.

effect: The cells rebuild fat and package it into chylomicrons; the remaining step is to send them into lymph.
reaction: The explanation makes the unfamiliar term chylomicrons useful, although the reason for the lymph route is still unclear.
reason: Use the lacteal entrance to complete the fat transport route.
expectation: Chylomicrons will enter the villus's central lymph vessel, though the mechanism is uncertain.

effect: Chylomicrons enter the villus lymph vessel and travel onward to blood, completing the fat route and both goals.
reaction: The destination is clear, but why these particles enter lymph rather than blood capillaries remains unexplained.

mostWorthwhile.text: Packaging absorbed fat into chylomicrons and sending them into lymph made the contrast with the glucose and amino-acid blood route concrete.

leastWorthwhile.text: The parallel glucose and amino-acid crossings were clear but repetitive; neither explained how the molecules cross the intestinal cells.

surprise.text: Intestinal cells rebuild fat before packaging it into chylomicrons, which enter lymph before reaching blood.

arbitrary.text: Combining glucose and amino acids already in villus blood felt like bookkeeping rather than a physical process, although it showed their shared route toward the liver.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how the absorbed nutrients are used, though I would want more explanation of the transport mechanisms and why fat takes the lymph route.
